entry.title: Combined summary - Re: RFC: Two years of BIP Editing, time for some new faces?
entry.summary: Over the past two years, the Bitcoin Improvement Proposals (BIPs) repository has undergone substantial development and revitalization. The concerted efforts of a six-member team of BIP Editors have resulted in thousands of community interactions, the processing of hundreds of pull requests, and the successful publication of dozens of new proposals. These achievements are underscored by enhancements to the proposal process itself, updates to documentation, and improvements to the supporting infrastructure such as continuous integration scripts. While the collaborative spirit among editors has been crucial, much of the workload has at times rested on a single individual, highlighting the demanding nature of this stewardship and reaffirming the need for a balanced distribution of editorial responsibilities. A more streamlined editorial team, ideally consisting of three highly engaged contributors, is advocated as an effective model for managing the BIPs repository. This structure promotes accountability, responsiveness, and sustained quality in the review and maintenance of proposals. Recognition is extended to key individuals whose dedication has played a vital role in elevating the repository’s standards, ensuring both visible progress and essential behind-the-scenes work that supports the project’s organization and momentum. The position of BIP Editor requires deep technical expertise with the Bitcoin protocol, including proficiency in relevant programming languages such as C++ and Python, as well as comprehensive knowledge of consensus mechanisms and open-source collaboration practices. Strong written communication skills and familiarity with tools like Git are essential for navigating the complexities of proposal submissions and feedback. Individuals aspiring to this role are expected to demonstrate prior involvement in Bitcoin projects or protocol design, meticulous attention to detail, and fluency in English. A commitment of five to ten hours per week is typical, with flexibility for additional time based on workload. Responsibilities include monitoring open pull requests, coordinating reviews, prompting updates from authors, and merging finalized changes. While editors lead the review process for new BIPs, proposal owners are generally responsible for reviewing modifications to their own work. Many tasks associated with BIP editing are accessible to all community members, encouraging broad participation and fostering a transparent, collaborative development environment. Interested parties can begin contributing by reviewing current open pull requests found at [this link](https://github.com/bitcoin/bips/pulls?q=is%3Aopen+is%3Apr+-label%3A%22Metadata+Update%22+-label%3ATypo-to-be-collected+-label%3ACI). Open contributions to the BIP repository are encouraged and valued, as constructive peer review strengthens both the quality of proposals and the overall trust in the editorial process. Community engagement through thoughtful feedback is recognized as an important pathway to editorial roles, with active and consistent participation serving as a strong endorsement of a candidate’s suitability for greater responsibility. The pace of activity within the BIP process may be gradual, but sustained input from diverse contributors remains crucial for maintaining high standards and advancing the protocol. Managing the growing workload associated with BIP reviews presents ongoing challenges, particularly when editor availability fluctuates due to travel or other commitments. High-quality proposals may remain unreviewed for extended periods, demonstrating the importance of expanding editorial capacity. To address concerns about long-term commitments, prospective volunteers are encouraged to consider limited terms—such as one or two years—thus making the role more approachable for qualified candidates who might otherwise hesitate to commit indefinitely. Maintaining rigorous standards in the BIP process is essential for the continued evolution and security of the Bitcoin protocol. Rather than compromising on review quality to meet resource constraints, the preferred strategy involves regularly refreshing the editorial team with dedicated new contributors. Increased allocation of working hours and adoption of academic-style peer review practices contribute to more thorough evaluation and clearer technical documentation. Notable recent initiatives, such as output descriptors and Miniscript, detailed in [Inside a Vinteum Deep Dive: The Standards Behind Bitcoin Wallets](https://www.vinteum.org/blog/inside-a-vinteum-deep-dive-the-standards-behind-bitcoin-wallets), as well as Stratum V2, discussed in [Inside a Vinteum Deep Dive: Bitcoin Mining from Protocol to Silicon](https://www.vinteum.org/blog/inside-a-vinteum-deep-dive-bitcoin-mining-from-protocol-to-silicon), exemplify the commitment to advancing best practices in specification and review. Contributors like Daniela Brozzoni have provided exemplary service through editorial diligence and attention to specification clarity, setting a benchmark for future BIP editors. Daniela Brozzoni has emerged as a strong candidate for the BIP Editor role, bringing direct experience as the author of BIP 394 and contributor to BIP 360. Her academic background in blockchain and ongoing involvement in reviewing Bitcoin Core contributions, as seen on her [GitHub profile](https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pulls?q=is%3Apr+reviewed-by%3Ajeanpablojp), underscore her readiness and commitment to the community.
